To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“We have prepared locus-specific immunological reagents for HLA-DR and -DQ by the production of monoclonal antibodies against the N-terminal sequences of each polypetide.
we have developed a new approach to produce antibodies to the β chains of the HLA‐D region.
we have produced antibodies to the HLA‐DR β chain and to the HLA DQ β chain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of immunologic reagents for the detection of HLA antigens on cells.
the development of new reagents to distinguish the HLA‐DR from the HLA‐Dq antigens.
the development of immunological reagents that can be used to distinguish between HLA‐DR, ‐DQ and ‐DP class II antigens and their products.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HLA‐DR antigens are a family of molecules that are encoded by a series of related genes.
the present study has demonstrated that it is possible to produce locus‐specific antibodies to the β chains of H‐LA‐DQ by immunization with the N‐terminal octopeptide of the molecule.
the present results demonstrate the possibility to prepare antibodies against synthetic peptides representing N‐terminal sequences in class II antigens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HLA‐D region is a cluster of genes encoding a series of closely related polypeptides, which can be divided into two groups, the HLA‐DP and HLA‐Dq, DR and DT antigens.
we have produced antibodies that can distinguish between HLA‐DR1 and ‐DQ1 and between HLA‐Dw4 and ‐DQw3.
we were the first group in the world to prepare antibodies against synthetic peptides of the HLA‐DR β chain and to show their use in immunological techniques.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N‐terminal octamers of HLA‐DP, ‐DQ and ‐DP β chains are highly immunogenic and the antibodies produced against them can be used to discriminate between HLA‐DR, ‐DQ, ‐DP and ‐DP β chain molecules.
the N‐terminal octamers are useful for the preparation of antibodies to the β chain of HLA‐DP, DR and DQ.

the N‐terminal octamers of HLA‐DP and ‐DQ are highly conserved in the population, and therefore, the antibodies against these octamers can detect a broad array of HLA‐class II alleles, and are thus potentially useful for the detection of HLA class II antigens in a broad population.
